title: HPA & KEDA tuning postmortem: conflicting metrics causing scale oscillation and cold-start regressions
creator: Marina Ortiz
description: Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed repeated capacity oscillations across several Dedicated clusters during a customer load test. Autoscalers (KEDA ScaledObjects + Kubernetes HPAs) performed conflicting decisions that resulted in premature scale-downs, a surge of cold-starts, and elevated latency for synchronous API traffic. This ticket documents the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.
impact: 3 production customers observed >500ms tail latency increases; 12% of in-flight requests during the peak window experienced transient failures/retries. SLA guardrails flagged a brief SLO breach for p99 latency on generation endpoints. No data loss; telemetry and logs retained.
root_cause: Regression & config mismatch: a metrics exporter change (ENG-9361) altered the queue-length metric name and intermittently reset metric series during exporter restarts. KEDA ScaledObjects were configured to use the obsolete metric name via an external Prometheus trigger, causing KEDA to see zero/absent values and trigger scale-downs. Simultaneously, the HPA was using a CPU/memory-based custom metric with a mis-set target resulting in slow scale-up. The combination produced conflicting scaling signals and an overall insufficient replica count during sustained load.
timeline: 2026-03-08 09:12 UTC - Load test begins (customer sandbox). Grafana detects p95/p99 increases.
2026-03-08 09:18 UTC - Automated alerts: autoscaler activity spike; ops channel alerted.
2026-03-08 09:22 UTC - KEDA triggered multiple scale-down events due to absent Prometheus metric (exporter restart coincident).
2026-03-08 09:25 UTC - HPA attempted scale-up but rate/target constrained; new pods cold-started and queued requests increased.
2026-03-08 09:30 UTC - Traffic spikes, p99 latency peaked; customers report errors. Incident declared P0.
2026-03-08 09:45 UTC - Emergency mitigation: ops pinned KEDA ScaledObject minReplicaCount to preserve baseline capacity and bumped HPA target. Immediate error rate reduced.
2026-03-08 11:00 UTC - Post-incident triage meeting; engineering assigned to root cause analysis and durable fixes.
actions: Short-term mitigation applied (done) — set minReplicaCount=3 on affected ScaledObjects across clusters — Owner: Devon Park — Completed: 2026-03-08
Rollback blocking change (done) — revert ENG-9361 metric name change to restore stable series while fix is developed — Owner: Priya Menon — Completed: 2026-03-09
Fix exporter to emit stable metric series and implement backpressure marker (in progress) — PR: github.com/redwood/metrics/PR-1824 — Owner: Carlos Vega — Due: 2026-03-17
Consolidate scaling signals (planned) — create a single canonical metric and update ScaledObjects + HPA to have deterministic precedence rules — Owner: Devon Park — Due: 2026-03-20

Tune cooldowns and stabilization windows (planned) — increase KEDA 'pollingInterval' and 'cooldownPeriod' and set HPA behavior stabilizationWindowSeconds to 60 — Owner: SRE Team (lead: Aisha Campbell) — Due: 2026-03-18
Implement canary rollout for metrics exporter changes (planned) — gating merges by integration test that simulates exporter restart behavior — Owner: QA/CI Team — Due: 2026-04-01
Add synthetic workload test to CI that validates scale-up latency and cold-start tail before release (planned) — Owner: Performance Team (lead: Marco Liu) — Due: 2026-03-31

Update runbook and incident playbook (done/in review) — document steps for minReplica quick-fix and how to interpret KEDA vs HPA metrics — Owner: Marina Ortiz — Completed draft: 2026-03-10; Review: 2026-03-13
notes: Observation: KEDA treats missing metrics as zero; our ScaledObjects relied on a metric that can briefly disappear during exporter restarts. We must never rely on ephemeral metric names without monotonic series behavior.
Decision: Move to a canonical 'queue_inflight' metric that uses stable labels and a cardinality contract documented for consumers.

Trade-offs: Increasing minReplica reduces cost-efficiency for low-traffic clusters. We'll scope minReplica changes only to high-SLA clusters and add an autoscale policy override in the Console for customers who opt-in.
Follow-up: Evaluate KEDA v2 (if available) for improved resiliency to metric gaps and check community recommendations for cooldown heuristics.
review_comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Campbell: Recommend adding a regression test that restarts the exporter mid-load and asserts KEDA does not scale-down below minReplica.
